result.title: Robust Counterfactuals for Markov Decision Processes under Statistical and Causal Uncertainties
result.summary: Counterfactual reasoning (asking what would have happened, had a decision been different) is a powerful tool for identifying causes of failure and explaining the behaviour of AI systems in sequential decision-making tasks. In Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), two sources of uncertainty complicate counterfactual inference: statistical uncertainty in the MDP transitions when the MDP is estimated from trajectory data, and uncertainty about the unknown causal model, as there are multiple structural causal models (SCMs) compatible with each MDP. Existing work addresses these two challenges in isolation. We address both simultaneously by introducing a framework for partial counterfactual inference in MDPs that is robust to both statistical and causal uncertainty. Our approach provides: 1) closed-form analytical bounds for the counterfactual probabilities that are valid across all SCMs entailed by a given interval MDP (IMDP); 2) a method to compute minimal robust interventions to achieve a desired counterfactual outcome via pessimistic value iteration on the induced counterfactual IMDP. Since the latter is constructed using our analytical bounds, our approach remains efficient and scalable to realistic MDP environments. Experiments across multiple case studies demonstrate our method's robustness and practical utility for identifying minimal sets of actions that, if changed, would have led to improved outcomes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对从轨迹数据估计的 MDP，同时处理转移的统计不确定性与未知因果模型（多个 SCM）的不确定性，提出部分反事实推断框架：给出对所有兼容 SCM 均成立的反事实概率闭式界，并通过在反事实 IMDP 上的悲观值迭代计算达成目标结果的最小鲁棒干预。
AI.relevance_reason: 其反事实归因、最小干预集与鲁棒界的思路，可能为 LVR 中判断哪些 latent 推理步骤或视觉证据真正导致答案变化、以及做因果抽象与贡献分配提供可核查的借鉴，但原文限于 MDP 序列决策，与 VLM 推理的关联尚属推测。
